poster_title: Reimagining Research Papers As Interactive and Reliable AI Agents
authors: Jiacheng Miao, Joe R. Davis, Yaohui Zhang, Jonathan K. Pritchard, and James Zou

panels.headline: Research papers are traditionally passive objects.
content: Papers require substantial effort to understand and adapt.
Technical barriers limit the accessibility and usability of new methods.
Advances in AI agents and LLMs promise more interactive and accessible research.

panels.headline: Technical barriers prevent easy use of new methods.
content: Executable papers improve reproducibility but still require technical expertise.
Current solutions do not fully address the need for interactive research tools.

panels.headline: Paper2Agent turns research papers into interactive AI agents.
content: Analyzes paper and associated codebase to construct MCP server.
Links MCP server to LLM-based chat agents for natural-language interaction.
panels.figure_caption: Overview of the Paper2Agent framework and workflow.

panels.headline: AlphaGenome agent achieved 100% accuracy on novel queries.
content: Agents created for AlphaGenome, ScanPy, and TISSUE.
Agents validated to reproduce original results and handle new queries.
panels.figure_caption: Overview of the AlphaGenome agent and its benchmarking results.

panels.headline: Agents could reproduce results and handle complex scientific queries.
content: Paper2Agent created reliable paper agents for genomic and transcriptomics analyses.
An AI co-scientist identified a new splicing variant associated with ADHD risk.
panels.figure_caption: Overview of the TISSUE agent and its Q&A support for spatial transcriptomics analysis.

panels.headline: Paper2Agent introduces a new paradigm for knowledge dissemination.
content: Framework lowers barriers to adoption and accelerates research translation.
Paper2Agent is a foundation for the collaborative ecosystem of AI co-scientists.
